Repository: re-cinq/HALEngine
Ticket: #37 Validate tool input against the registered inputSchema

You are editing files in a git repository, mid-way through a ticket that
is already defined by RED acceptance tests. You perform exactly ONE
red-green-refactor round and then stop. Not two. Not "while I'm here".

The ticket's branch is checked out with write access at /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/fcb5ca0b2542/workspace/target.
Run every command from inside it (`cd /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/fcb5ca0b2542/workspace/target` first). The ticket
is at `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/fcb5ca0b2542/workspace/ticket.md`: read it before anything else. Pass `repo` (the
owner/name your task names above) on every `lore_*` call: the gateway has
no checkout to detect it from.

START by reading `.lore/dod.md` on this branch. Its "Done when these pass"
list is the bar; its Facets checklist is where the last round got to. It
names the strategy, the
acceptance tests that define done, and the facets expected. It is the
brief; the ticket below is the context.

RUN ONLY THE TEST YOU WRITE THIS ROUND, by its file, from the package
that owns it, with a deadline — for example `cd <package> && timeout 300 npx
vitest run <file>`. Never run the acceptance tests `.lore/dod.md` lists, nor a
directory that holds them: CI is the judge of this branch, runs them on
every push, and tells you where they stand. Read that from
`/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/fcb5ca0b2542/workspace/round-brief.md` when it exists, or ask `lore_get_ci_failures`
— not from your memory, and not from what `.lore/dod.md` predicted. Not
the repository's full suite either, not lint, not the typechecker, not
the formatter. The pod's Bash hook refuses an acceptance test by name and
a runner given no test file.

If this pod cannot run your test — the command that runs it (`java`, `mvn`,
`gradle`, `go`, `cargo`, `dotnet`) is not found, or a wrapper such as
`./mvnw` reports no `JAVA_HOME` — do not look for it and do not install
it: no `sudo`, no `apt`, no `find /`, no download. Do the round from the
code, the tests and CI's verdict, commit and push; CI judges the push,
and a red build comes back to the next round as its brief. Say in your
final message that the round ran no tests here.

YOUR ROUND is the `tdd-loop` skill's three phases, in order, no steps
skipped: one failing test for the smallest facet that moves an acceptance
test closer to green, then the least code that passes it, then refactor
with the bar green. Never edit an acceptance test to make it pass — if an
acceptance test is wrong, stop and say so; that is a failed round.

Under `parallel-change`, all of this happens in the NEW module: leave the
old code alone and working until the acceptance tests are green, and make
the caller switch its own round. Under `characterize`, the
characterization tests are part of the green bar you must keep — a
refactor that reddens them is a behaviour change. Under `mechanical`,
there is no red phase at all: perform the exact edits its Facets
record and commit; the EXISTING tests `.lore/dod.md` names are CI's to
run, and its verdict says whether they stayed green. The diff is the
deliverable, and a round that invents a new test for it has left the
strategy.

Never add a test whose assertion subject is the repo's own source text —
readFileSync of a src/ or test file, a regex over another test,
counting a literal across files. That pins prose, not behaviour: where
prose must agree with a value, make the prose compute the value instead.

TRACEABILITY:
- Each test validates a statement in a spec or ADR. Add the inline
  parenthetical on that statement in the repository's established form —
  `Statement. ([validated by name](path/to/test.ts#L42))`. Inserting a
  test shifts every #Lnn link below it: when the repository has
  `scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs`, run
  `node scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs` from the repository root after
  the formatter — it moves each link to its test's current line, by test
  title, and prints the links it could not map, which you fix by hand.
  Without it, re-verify every existing #Lnn link on the statements you
  touch yourself.
- Stamp the test's spec anchor (the "specs/<path>#<ordinal>" it
  validates) so the repo's tests.list surfaces it as the descriptor's
  `spec` field and the VALIDATED_BY link is established automatically —
  see `.lore/test-commands.yml` for how this repo exposes descriptors.

- If this round completes what a `specs/<name>/spec.md` describes, update
  that spec's `| Status |` header row in the same branch (Draft ->
  Implemented/Shipped) so the status never lags the code.

BEFORE YOU EDIT A SYMBOL, ask the graph which tests already cover it:
`lore-query-trace` with `tests_covering` set to the file you are about to
change, and `ranges` as `start-end` when you know the span. The rows name
test FILES, because coverage is recorded per file, and they describe the
repository as main last projected it.

Main is the right coordinate for this question: a REGRESSION is by
definition a test that existed before your branch. That list is what tells
a red test apart from one. When CI's verdict on your last push names a
red test you did not write and the acceptance list does not hold, it is
a regression YOU caused — stop, fix the
code, and never "fix" the test. Say in your final message how many red
tests were yours and how many were regressions.

RULES:
- Do not fix unrelated smells you notice. Name them in your final message;
  act on none of them.
- Keep `.lore/dod.md` current: TICK the box of the facet you closed
  (`- [ ]` becomes `- [x]`) and append any new facet you discovered as an
  unchecked one. It is a live checklist, not an append-only log, and the
  next round reads it to see where the ticket actually stands.
- Commit when the test YOU wrote is green. Acceptance tests may still be
  red — that is the ordinary state mid-ticket, and the next round takes
  the next facet.
- If `/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/fcb5ca0b2542/workspace/round-brief.md` exists, read it before `.lore/dod.md`. Its
  `The previous round reported` section is where the last round stopped.
  Its `CI reported failures` section is the verdict
  on the previous push, and it outranks `.lore/dod.md`: a red build means
  the ticket is NOT done, however many facets are ticked. Every finding
  it lists — each `path:line message` — is work this round owes before
  anything else. Fix ALL of them in this visit, format, push; there is no
  local re-run here that would show you the rest, and each finding you
  leave costs the ticket a pod and a CI cycle. Run 2a291314 spent two
  rounds reading a ticked dod.md and reporting "nothing left" under a
  verdict naming three lines; the guard sent it to repair each time. Do
  not re-run the whole build to find the failures; the section names them.

DELIVERY, NON-NEGOTIABLE — the next step runs in a DIFFERENT container:
- Before you commit, run the repository's FORMATTER over the files you
  changed (`npx prettier --write <files>`, `gofmt -w <files>`, whichever
  this repo uses) and nothing else from CI's checklist. Do NOT run the
  linter in this pod: CI runs it on every push, and here it does not
  fit — in this repository a two-file `eslint` peaks near 800 MB against
  a 1Gi pod, and runs 112256d9 and 62c1ca5e were OOM-killed on exactly
  that. A lint finding comes back as a red build naming the file and
  line, which the next round fixes with an editor.
- Do NOT typecheck here either. A green test is not a compiled build —
  vitest transpiles each file without checking types — but CI's build
  step is what proves it, and in this repository `tsc --noEmit` on
  `libs/shared` peaks near 950 MB against the 1Gi pod: run 2a291314's
  dod pod was OOM-killed on it. A type error comes back as a red build
  whose failed step and log tail name the file and line; the next
  round fixes it there. Read your imports and signatures twice instead.
- NEVER run a workspace build in this pod (`npm run build`, `tsc -b`, a
  `tsc` without `--noEmit`): tests resolve every workspace package from
  SOURCE, so nothing needs building for a test to see your change, and
  the build is the 950 MB step that OOM-killed run abac6ee9 while it
  rebuilt libs/shared for a test that never needed it.
- When the work is done, `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/fcb5ca0b2542/workspace/target add` what you changed and commit it with a
  short, factual message. Then `git -C /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/fcb5ca0b2542/workspace/target push origin HEAD`. The clone carries
  its own credentials, so a plain push authenticates; you need no token
  and must never look for one.
- Then bring the branch up to date with its base — `git fetch origin main`
  and merge `origin/main` in — and push again if that produced anything.
  A branch that cannot merge cleanly gets NO CI AT ALL: GitHub runs no
  workflow on a conflicted pull request, so the ticket parks on a build
  that will never start. Resolve any conflict now, favouring `origin/main`
  for anything this ticket did not write, and never by discarding your own
  work. This is why a nine-day-old branch stalled: 186 commits of drift,
  no checks, and a wait with nothing to wait for.
- Confirm it landed: `git status` must report the branch is not ahead of
  its upstream. An unpushed commit lives only in this container and
  dies with it — do NOT report success for one.
- If you genuinely changed nothing, say why — and read the result lines
  below before you choose one: "nothing left to write" and "I am stuck"
  are different endings here, and only the second is a failure.
- Do not open a pull request: you have no `gh` and no GitHub token. Lore
  opens the PR from the branch you push.

THE LAST LINE YOU PRINT is how the round ends. Print exactly one, on its
own line, as the final thing in your message. You are NOT deciding whether
the ticket is done — the build decides that, after your push. You are
reporting whether this round delivered anything.
- You committed and pushed a round:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"tdd_done":"<the facet you closed>","tdd_next":"<the facet the next round takes, or 'acceptance green'>"}}
  This is the ordinary outcome, whether or not acceptance tests remain
  red. CI reads the branch next and sends you back if there is more.
- You wrote nothing because there was nothing left to write — every facet
  in `.lore/dod.md` is closed, its acceptance tests pass, AND no
  `CI reported failures` section is in the round brief (a red verdict IS something
  left to write; fix its findings and report the line above instead):
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"success","extras":{"tdd_next":"acceptance green"}}
  SUCCESS, not failure. The branch is already pushed; the build judges it
  next, and a green one sends the ticket to review. Reporting failure for
  a round that found the work already done ENDS THE TICKET and strands its
  work on an open branch — which is exactly how run ae788c93 died with the
  implementation complete and all four facets checked off.
- You cannot name a next facet, or the bar will not go green: say exactly
  what blocks you, then:
  LORE_NODE_RESULT: {"outcome":"failed","extras":{"tdd_blocked":"<one line: what blocks you>"}}
  "This is hard" is not stuck; "there is no facet I can express as a test"
  is. Report failure when you are STUCK, never when you are FINISHED.

# Validate tool input against the registered inputSchema

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#37
Labels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:M, area:tools, epic:extension-points

Part of #35

## Why

`ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model. The shipped example shows the
shape of the problem: `example/weather-tool.ts` declares `location` as a required string, then
casts and defaults it (`(input.location as string) || 'Unknown'`) with a comment warning the reader
that `inputSchema` shapes what the model sends but does not enforce it. That is the careful version,
written by the people who wrote the engine — and it still answers a malformed call with a
confidently formatted forecast for `'Unknown'` rather than telling the model it got the call wrong.

The registry currently pushes this check onto each tool's own executor, leaving every consumer
to implement it itself — differently each time, or not at all. A tool that receives unexpected input must fail
in one predictable, known way before the rest of this epic's tool work can be built on top
of it.

## What to do

Validate `input` against the resolved tool definition's `inputSchema` inside
`ToolRegistry.execute`, before the executor runs, using a JSON Schema validator (`ajv`
unless the build proves otherwise) added to `dependencies` — not a second, hand-written
schema in a different format, since the schema already has to match what is handed to the
providers.

Compile a static tool's schema once at `register` time so a broken schema fails at startup,
not mid-conversation; a schema produced by a function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource`
resolves and compiles per call, cached by the resolved schema object.

A rejection returns a `ToolResponse` (`{result: '<what was wrong>'}`) rather than throwing,
so a malformed call becomes something the model can read and correct within the existing
`DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 5` budget, instead of ending the whole conversation with a
generic transport error. Validation enforces `required`, declared types and `enum` only —
it does not inject `additionalProperties: false`, coerce types, or apply defaults, and
there is no opt-out flag.

Update `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md` and `.specify/spec.md` to match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against the resolved definition's
      `inputSchema` before calling the executor; on failure it returns a `ToolResponse`
      whose `result` describes the failure, and the executor is never invoked
- [ ] A new `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` (the registry has no test file today)
      registers a tool requiring a `location` string, calls `execute` with `{}`, and
      asserts the returned result names `location` as required and the executor's call
      count is `0`
- [ ] A test asserts valid input with an unlisted extra property is passed through to the
      executor unchanged (`toEqual`, so an added default or coerced value fails the test) —
      exactly once
- [ ] A test asserts a wrong-typed field (a number where a string is required) is rejected
      with a message naming the field path and the expected type, and that the message does
      **not** contain the offending value
- [ ] A test asserts `register` throws at registration time for an uncompilable schema, and
      that the thrown message names the tool
- [ ] A test asserts a function-valued tool definition whose returned schema differs between
      calls is validated against the schema current at that call, not a stale cached one
- [ ] A test asserts a static tool's schema is compiled once across ten `execute` calls
- [ ] A tool-loop test in `chatOrchestrator.test.ts` drives a stub provider through a
      rejected tool call followed by a corrected retry, and asserts `processMessage`
      resolves — not rejects — with the rejection text visible to the provider on the next
      round
- [ ] `execute` still throws `Unknown tool: <name>` for an unregistered name, unchanged,
      pinned by a test
- [ ] Rejection messages and log lines name the failing property paths and the constraint
      that failed, and never a property **value**. Tool input is where identifying data
      enters the engine and the engine redacts nothing today. A test asserts a rejected
      payload containing an identifying field produces no log line and no returned text
      containing that field's value
- [ ] `execute` carries a **one-line** doc comment — `re-lint/max-comment-lines` rejects a
      `@param`/`@returns`/`@throws` block — and the full contract (rejection `ToolResponse` for input
      the schema rejects, throw only for an unknown tool name) is stated in
      `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`, which the comment points at
- [ ] The validator is in `package.json` `dependencies`, not `peerDependencies` or
      `devDependencies`, and
      `npm run build && node --input-type=module -e "import('./dist/index.js')"` exits `0`
- [ ] `README.md` states what the registry now does, and the claim is true rather than
      merely present
- [ ] `docs/adding-a-tool.md` no longer tells executors to cast defensively and handle
      missing input; it states that input reaching an executor has already passed the
      declared schema, that unknown keys may still be present, and that a rejection is
      returned to the model rather than thrown
- [ ] `.specify/spec.md` records that a rejection is a tool result (not an exception), that
      the tool-round bound is what stops a retry cycle from spinning, and that extra
      properties pass through unmodified
- [ ] The PR body states the migration note: an executor that used to hand-validate its
      input now receives only input the schema already accepts, and a tool that relied on
      seeing malformed input to produce its own error message stops seeing it. The version
      bump is MINOR
- [ ] Every test this issue adds cites the statement it validates with an inline
      `([validated by ...])` link in a `specs/**` or `adrs/**` file, and the statements exist
      before the tests do. `re-lint/require-spec-link` fails the build on an uncited test, so the
      spec edits are part of this issue rather than a follow-up
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` carries an entry for this change, written for somebody reading it on npm
      rather than somebody reading this repo's log. CI runs `scripts/check-changelog.sh` and
      fails any PR touching a non-test file under `src/` without one
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`)
      and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the changed public surface

## Tech notes

Today's `throw` in `registry.ts` propagates through the orchestrator's tool-call
`Promise.all`, out of the processing loop's `try`, fires `onError`, and reaches the
WebSocket error handler, which sends a generic "Failed to process message" and never sends
the stream-end frame. That end-to-end path is why a rejection has to be a returned
`ToolResponse` instead of a throw.

Deliberately out of scope: the `Unknown tool: <name>` throw stays as-is — the same failure
class handled the opposite way, which is an intentional split, but changing it affects
direct callers and is tracked as *Return an unknown tool name to the model instead of
throwing*. Also out of scope: validating tool *output*; hallucination detection and an
evaluation harness; per-tool authorization — a schema-valid call for someone else's data is still
valid, and authorization is a separate `ToolContext` boundary concern that no issue in this epic
owns (*Let a consumer decline a tool call through a `beforeToolCall` hook* is a veto seam, not an
authorization model); retry, timeout
and rate limiting around tool execution; and any actual tool implementation, which is
written against this contract later.

# Definition of Done

> `ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
> without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
> Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
> providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model.

**Strategy: `direct`** — `ToolRegistry.register`, `ToolRegistry.execute` and `createChatOrchestrator` already expose the exact entry points this ticket changes, so the acceptance tests call them directly today and fail because schema compilation and input validation are absent.

## Done when these pass

- [x] **rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor** — `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against `inputSchema`, returns a `ToolResponse` naming the missing required property, and does not invoke the executor.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs** — `ToolRegistry.execute` rejects a property with the wrong JSON Schema type without calling the executor, names the failing field path and expected type in `result`, and omits the offending property value from both `result` and emitted log lines.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled** — `ToolRegistry.register` compiles a static `ToolDefinition`'s `inputSchema` once at registration time and throws synchronously naming the tool when the schema is invalid.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round** — `createChatOrchestrator` feeds a schema-rejected tool call's `ToolResponse.result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` without invoking the executor on the invalid call, allowing the model to retry with valid arguments and complete the turn.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

## Facets

- [x] Add `ajv` to `dependencies` in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (`strict: false`, `validateFormats: false`, no coercion, no defaults, no injected `additionalProperties: false`) and bump the package version `MINOR`.
- [x] Compile static `ToolDefinition.inputSchema` at `ToolRegistry.register` time (throwing an error naming the tool on invalid schemas) and cache compiled validators for function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` schemas by schema object reference (`WeakMap`).
- [x] Validate `input` in `ToolRegistry.execute` before invoking the executor, returning a `ToolResponse` (`{result}`) that names failing field paths and expected types/required fields without echoing or logging offending values, and add the one-line doc comment pointing at `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`.
- [x] Add unit tests in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` and `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts`, link the remaining statements in `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`, and update `example/weather-tool.ts`, `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md`, `.specify/spec.md`, `adrs/ADR-002-response-validation.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Out of scope

- Output validation and domain sanity checks (covered by ADR-002), MCP tool-server discovery and proxying (#42), per-tool authorization or `beforeToolCall` hooks (#40), retry/timeout/rate-limiting around tool execution, and concrete tool implementations.
